_about: LeetCode practice list. Only number, title, difficulty, topic, link, and my own short hints. No problem statements are copied.

problems.title: Two Sum
problems.hint: As you walk through the list, remember each number you have seen. For each new number, ask whether the value that would complete the target is already in your memory.

problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.hint: If you keep track of every value you've seen, you'll know the moment one shows up a second time.

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.hint: Two words are anagrams when every letter appears the same number of times in both.

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.keyIdea: Hash map with a computed key
problems.hint: Anagrams look identical once their letters are sorted (or counted). Use that as the key for grouping.

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.hint: Count how often each value appears first. Then you only need the k largest counts, which a heap or buckets indexed by count can give you.

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.hint: The answer at each position is (product of everything to its left) times (product of everything to its right). Build both in two passes.

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.hint: Skip anything that isn't a letter or digit, compare without caring about case, and move inward from both ends.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.hint: Start with the widest pair. The shorter side limits the area, so moving that side inward is the only move that could help.

problems.title: 3Sum
problems.hint: Sort first. Fix one number, then search the rest for a matching pair with two pointers. Skip repeated values to avoid duplicate answers.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.keyIdea: One pass with a running minimum
problems.hint: Keep track of the lowest price so far. On each day, check what the profit would be if you sold today.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.hint: Keep a window with no repeated characters. When a repeat appears, move the left edge just past the earlier copy.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.hint: Every closing bracket has to match the most recent opening bracket that is still unmatched.

problems.title: Min Stack
problems.keyIdea: Stack that also stores the minimum
problems.hint: Next to each value, also store what the minimum was at that moment, so popping never loses track of it.

problems.title: Daily Temperatures
problems.hint: Keep a stack of days that are still waiting for a warmer day. A warmer temperature answers every colder day on top of the stack.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.hint: Compare with the middle element and throw away the half that can't contain the target.

problems.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.hint: At any middle point, at least one half is still sorted. Check if the target falls inside that sorted half to decide where to go next.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.hint: Walk the list and turn each next pointer around. Save a reference to the rest of the list before you change it.

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.hint: Use a placeholder starting node and keep attaching the smaller of the two current nodes.

problems.title: Linked List Cycle
problems.hint: Move one pointer one step at a time and another two steps at a time. If there is a loop, they will meet.

problems.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.hint: The depth of a tree is 1 plus the depth of its deeper subtree.

problems.title: Invert Binary Tree
problems.hint: Swap the left and right children of every node.

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.hint: Process the tree one level at a time with a queue. The queue's size at the start of each round tells you how many nodes are on that level.

problems.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
problems.hint: Each node has to fit inside a range set by all of its ancestors, not only its parent.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.hint: Each time you find land you haven't visited, count one island and mark all the land connected to it as visited.

problems.title: Clone Graph
problems.hint: Keep a map from each original node to its copy, so you never copy a node twice and cycles don't loop forever.

problems.title: Course Schedule
problems.hint: Courses and prerequisites form a directed graph. All courses can be finished only if that graph has no cycle.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problems.hint: Keep a min-heap that never holds more than k items. After going through everything, the smallest item in the heap is the answer.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.hint: To reach step n, your last move came from step n-1 or step n-2.

problems.title: House Robber
problems.hint: At each house, pick the better of two choices: skip it, or take it plus the best total from two houses back.

problems.title: Coin Change
problems.hint: For every amount from 0 up to the target, the fewest coins is 1 plus the best answer for (amount minus a coin), tried over every coin.

problems.title: Recyclable and Low Fat Products
problems.hint: Two conditions have to be true at the same time. Combine them in the WHERE clause.

problems.title: Combine Two Tables
problems.hint: Every row from the first table has to appear, even without a match. Which join keeps all rows from the left side?

problems.title: Duplicate Emails
problems.hint: Group rows by the value and keep only the groups that appear more than once.

problems.title: Customers Who Never Order
problems.keyIdea: Anti-join (LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL, or NOT EXISTS)
problems.hint: You want rows with no match in the other table. A LEFT JOIN where the right side is NULL is one way; NOT EXISTS is another.

problems.title: Employees Earning More Than Their Managers
problems.hint: Join the table to itself: one copy plays the employee, the other copy plays the manager.

problems.title: Rising Temperature
problems.hint: Pair each day with the day before it by joining the table to itself on a one-day difference. Check how your SQL dialect does date math.

problems.title: Second Highest Salary
problems.hint: Find the largest value that is smaller than the maximum. Think about what to return when there isn't one.

problems.title: Department Highest Salary
problems.keyIdea: GROUP BY in a subquery, or a window function
problems.hint: First find the top value per group, then return every row that matches it, so ties are kept.

problems.title: Tenth Line
problems.hint: Print only the line whose line number is 10. sed, awk, or head and tail can each do it.

problems.title: Valid Phone Numbers
problems.hint: Write one pattern for each allowed format, join them with |, and anchor the whole thing with ^ and $.

problems.title: Word Frequency
problems.hint: Put each word on its own line, count each word, then sort by the count from highest to lowest.

problems.title: Transpose File
problems.hint: Columns become rows. In awk, collect each field into an array keyed by its column number and print the array at the end.
